l.i: Quem mortuum lugent boni, horrescùt mali.
Ipfa a quo potuit Virtutem discere Virtus,
Cur adeo exiguo, ignotóque in cespite clausus
Hoc tumulo manibus condidit ipsa suis.
O te beatum cespitem tanto hospite! O
TE vivo, Caluine, fuit mihi vivere dulce,
Hei, quàm dulce foret, te moriente, mori!
Et tamen est, fateor, grata hoc mihi nomine vita,
Quod tibi quas fundam sufficiat lacrymas.
Vive igitur, Beza, in luctus, tibi ut vsque perenes
Caluini in tumulum vita ministret aquas:
Iunctura absenti donec te rursus amico,

page.notes: The large initials R (of "Roma") and T (of "TE") are drop caps; read as ROma and TE. Some long-s and u/v forms were normalised as the rules require. Lines with a broken or unclear letter were read from the scan with best effort; no [?] marks were needed on clear words. The catchword EX sits alone at the lower right.
